questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
The size (small town, which often means lower prices and a chill vibe)
The area (Toscana, which is a nice region, reachable by train from Denmark but still a bit to the south)
I study italian language and culture, so of course I wanted to go to Italy

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
I really enjoyed my life in Pisa, but the quality of the education/the university of Pisa, was not the best.
It had som nice libraries though, and the professors were also nice, but not all of them were very good at teaching.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Some of it was pretty easy, but the Online Learning Agreement, the course catalogue and the information about how the online platforms/the system of the university worked, was hard to figure out.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was a welcome meeting which was useful, but other than that, not much. Besides, the responsibles, who also made the welcome meeting, were not good at helping with The Online Learning Agreement and official enrollment.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was pretty easy, I joined an italian Facebook group around four months before I left, which worked out well.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: They should ask their host if they need to bring bed linnen and stuff like that for the bed, because apparently not all hosts have it availible when you arrive.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I really liked the place I lived. The price was also good.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: You should get a proper tutorial for this. The italian system is not easy to navigate.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You could write a mail to the administrator of the exchange students, which helped

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very succesful.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't be nervous about it if it doesn't work out at first. You will figure it out once you arrive, it's not that urgent. Read the descriptions of the courses thoroughly, so you actually know what you're signing up to learn about.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Two of the courses were on the second year, and one was on the first.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The style of teaching is much better in Copenhagen. The best professor I had used powerpoints, spoke clearly, and asked often if there were any questions. She also managed to keep a good structure, so you knew that you learned the thing you needed for the exam. This is similar to the style of teaching I'm used to.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Storia dell'estetica, Letteratura italiana 1, Storia e techniche della critica letteraria.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Storia dell'estetica, because the professor, Elena Romagnoli is good, and it's interesting.
I also enjoyed Storia e techniche della critica letteraria, but that was because of the texts/books on the programme. Not the professors.

Food DKK per month *

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I had to buy bed linnen, two duvets and towel, which I didn't expect.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: The train was more expensive than I thought, but generally it was cheaper to live in Pisa than in Copenhagen, so I can't complain.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There weren't a lot of these clubs, sports etc.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I don't know, it wasn't obvious and I didn't come across it.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Having coffee/a drink/a meal with the locals - talking to them, going to events with them.
The ESN activities.
Walking around the city/town alone.
Exploring the area.
Cooking healthy food at home.
Reading books from the country who are in, watching their tv-shows and listening/movies, listening to music in the language of the country.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Explore the area. Study. Go out. Read. Relax. Do what you feel like I guess?

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Sort of easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Just sit next to them in classes, or go to the same events, introduce yourself, be interested, polite, and take the initiative to grab a coffee or something.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Different eating schedules/habits, having to meet up late in the evening, a lack of structure

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The language, the food, drinks, young people not drinking to much every weekend, the beautiful old buildings, gesticulation/body language, politeness, the bars (which is also the word for cafés), the piazzas (squares where you hang out)...

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Make your own experiences<3
Bring warm sweaters and socks for late fall/winter/early spring, for the apartments are cold but also shorts, t-shirts and sandals for the late spring and summer, for Pisa can get extremely hot. 
Appreciate being able to walk everywhere, but get a bike if you live far from the center.
Learn a bit of italian and be polite ofc.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: If your professor is boring, change the course early on or prepare yourself to read more instead of going to all the classes.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: My italian has gotten better, I've grown to like being alone a lot more, I had some good experiences, made italian friends and I feel proud of myself for overcoming the challenges.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer:
Not understanding some of the professors very well, missing structure and information regarding the exams for example. 
Missing my partner and friends.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
